rules.quote: embed its token in the URL instead
rules.rule: When pushing to or cloning a GitHub repo over HTTPS on this machine, embed the gh CLI token in the URL (https://x-access-token:$(gh auth token)@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git) instead of relying on git's credential helper.

rules.quote:
clone with the token URL into the
scratchpad
rules.rule: For a one-off GitHub push, clone the repo using the token URL into the scratchpad directory.

rules.quote: remove the clone afterwards
rules.rule: After a one-off GitHub push, remove the scratchpad clone, since the token is stored in its .git/config.

rules.quote: Don't "fix" it by installing the helper without asking
rules.rule: Do not install the libsecret credential helper to fix GitHub HTTPS auth failures without first asking the user.

rules.quote: `kill -USR1 <pid>` still comes first
rules.rule: When glute hangs, send `kill -USR1 <pid>` to the process before doing anything else.

rules.quote: then read the dump in `glute.log`
rules.rule: After sending `kill -USR1`, read the goroutine dump in `glute.log` before killing the glute process.

rules.quote: `reset` restores it
rules.rule: If a killed glute run leaves the terminal in raw mode, run `reset` to restore it.

rules.quote: This is the direction to build on for stats
rules.rule: Build new stats features on the GraphQL client in `internal/gitlab/graphql.go`, not on new REST paths.

rules.quote: don't over-expect it when designing stats
rules.rule: When designing stats features, do not expect GitLab's GraphQL to aggregate server-side. Pull the records and aggregate them client-side.

rules.quote: must not fall through the cracks
rules.rule: Make sure projects that are alive only through forgotten scheduled pipelines are never skipped by the resync or poll logic.

rules.quote: sweep on `last_activity_at` is **rejected**
rules.rule: Do not gate the warm per-project sweep on `last_activity_at`.

rules.quote: unfit for the warm sweep
rules.rule: Do not use the group-level GraphQL `projects { pipelines(first:1, updatedAfter) }` query in the warm sweep. Use it only for a once-per-resync probe.

rules.quote: on `main`
rules.rule: Land glute work on the `main` branch.

rules.quote:
instrument the running app, gather real numbers, then
design the scheme from what the data actually shows.
rules.rule: When working on a performance task, instrument the running app and gather real measurements before designing any optimization.

rules.quote:
add lightweight timing/counters
first (per-phase, retained across runs, surfaced somewhere observable), run
against a realistic dataset, and let the breakdown choose the target.
rules.rule: For a nontrivial performance task, add lightweight per-phase timing/counters first, retained across runs and surfaced somewhere observable, then run against a realistic dataset and let the breakdown choose the optimization target.

rules.quote:
Keep the
instrumentation in afterward to confirm the win.
rules.rule: After a performance optimization, keep the instrumentation in place to confirm the improvement.

rules.quote:
Don't trust prior "this is the
slow part" claims — including ones written in the repo's own docs.
rules.rule: Do not trust prior claims that a particular part is the slow part, including claims written in the repo's own docs; verify with measurement.

rules.quote:
drive them
through a Makefile as the first choice
rules.rule: For projects with local, non-CI build steps or other processes, drive them through a Makefile as the first choice.

rules.quote:
with the default `make` target doing
the project's primary build.
rules.rule: For projects with local build steps, make the default `make` target perform the project's primary build.

rules.quote:
reach
for a Makefile before ad-hoc scripts, unless there is a concrete reason to do
otherwise.
rules.rule: When a project needs local build/dev/process automation, reach for a Makefile before ad-hoc scripts, unless there is a concrete reason to do otherwise.

rules.quote:
Before writing a memory or a CLAUDE.md note, ask whether it
would be fine on a public web page.
rules.rule: Before writing a memory or CLAUDE.md note, ask whether it would be fine on a public web page; if not, do not write it.

rules.quote: Keep out secrets and tokens
rules.rule: Keep secrets and tokens out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote:
software
versions of internal servers
rules.rule: Keep software versions of internal servers out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: runner and machine names
rules.rule: Keep runner and machine names out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote:
internal project
names
rules.rule: Keep internal project names out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: cloud account/subscription/zone ids
rules.rule: Keep cloud account, subscription, and zone ids out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: the scopes of Marcel's own tokens
rules.rule: Keep the scopes of the user's own tokens out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: local filesystem paths
rules.rule: Keep local filesystem paths out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote: facts about other projects
rules.rule: Keep facts about other projects out of memory files and CLAUDE.md.

rules.quote:
Cite a real-instance
example by its pipeline id ("pipeline #235448"), not its project.
rules.rule: When citing a real-instance example in memory files or CLAUDE.md, cite it by its pipeline id, not by its project name.

rules.quote:
Another
project's facts go in that project's own memory store, even when the session
that learned them was started here.
rules.rule: Store facts about another project in that project's own memory store, even if the session that learned them was started in this repo.
